statement: A tree is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its left and right children. Print the tree's maximum depth counted in nodes: the number of nodes on the longest chain from the root down to a leaf. Recurse with the leap of faith - the depth of an empty tree is 0, and the depth at any node is 1 plus the larger of its two subtree depths.
constraints: Node values are positive; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: The chain 1, 2, 4 holds three nodes; no chain in this tree is longer.

hint: One line of combine: 1 plus the max of the two child depths, with 0 for the empty tree.
mistake: Returning the max of the child depths with no +1 - every answer collapses to 0.
